entries.name: Your aircraft (overview, then one page per aircraft)

pages.title: About these charts
paragraphs: **Built from DCS, for DCS.** Every chart is drawn from the game itself: the pavement, buildings and parking stands from the F10 map, the runways, beacons and frequencies from the DCS World files, the ground from the terrain read in DCS. Taxiway names come from OpenStreetMap, or from the signs read in DCS. Where DCS and the real world disagree, the chart follows DCS: what you see on the chart is what you will find in the game.

**Two norths.** The top of every page is the north of the DCS map grid — the north of the F10 map. Every heading, bearing and radial printed on a chart is **magnetic**, computed for the year 1985. The magnetic variation is printed on each page (VAR 3°E at Konya): magnetic heading = grid heading − variation when it is east.

**Units.** Altitudes and elevations in feet; distances in nautical miles (NM); runway lengths in feet and metres. Helicopter pages add metres and kilometres, and heights above the airfield (QFE) in metres, for aircraft whose instruments are metric.
**What is not on the charts.** Minima (DCS publishes none), obstacles, real procedures. The approaches are standard patterns laid on the DCS beacons and the DCS terrain: plausible, not official.

**Where to get them.** One PDF per airfield in the repository (`downloads/`), and two zips per theatre attached to the latest release: every page as PDF, as PNG sized for the DCS kneeboard, and as SVG.

**On the kneeboard.** Copy the PNG pages of the airfields you need into `Saved Games\DCS\Kneeboard\` (pages for every aircraft) or into a subfolder of it named after one aircraft (pages for that aircraft only); older installations use `Saved Games\DCS.openbeta\`. The subfolder takes the module's name inside DCS, which is not always its commercial name. You can also attach the pages to the mission in the Mission Editor. Name them so they sort in the order you want (`01_…`, `02_…`).

pages.title: The pages of an airfield

thumbs.name: Vicinity
thumbs.line: The airfield in its surroundings, on the F10 map: to find it and recognise it.

thumbs.name: Airfield
thumbs.line: The airfield itself: runways, taxiways, frequencies, beacons.

thumbs.name: Parking
thumbs.line: Every parking stand with its DCS number, when the 10-9 has no room for them.

thumbs.name: Approach
thumbs.line: An instrument approach for aircraft, one runway direction per page.

thumbs.name: Approach
thumbs.line: The same for helicopters: NDB only, one altitude, metric heights.

pages.text: Not every airfield has every page. An airfield without its own beacon within 3 NM has no approach page. A helicopter base has a 10-8 and a 10-9; the other heliports are in the heliport directory (chapter 6). The PDF of an airfield holds all its pages in this order.

pages.title: Vicinity — 10-8 (Konya)

pins.title: Same header as the 10-9
pins.text: Elevation, position, variation, tower and navaids are repeated, so this page can be used alone.

pins.title: The F10 map, lightened
pins.text: Exactly what you see on the F10 map in the game, so you can match the two.

pins.title: Runways
pins.text: Each with its magnetic heading, at the threshold where you land.

pins.title: Beacons
pins.text: At their real place, with ident and frequency or channel.

pins.title: Towns within 20 km
pins.text: Off the page: a triangle at the edge, in the direction of the town, with its distance from the airfield.

pins.title: Latitude and longitude
pins.text: One tick per minute.

pins.title: Scale
pins.text: In feet and metres; the 10-8 covers a few kilometres around the airfield.

pins.title: Runway table
pins.text: As on the 10-9.

use: On arrival, the 10-8 tells you what the airfield looks like from the air: the town on one side, the motorway on the other, the shape of the runways.
With the F10 map open, the page and the map match: use them together to plan your join.
The towns at the edge give you a line feature to fly to before you see the runway.

pages.title: Airfield — 10-9 (Konya)

pins.title: Airfield
pins.text: ICAO code (when it has one), DCS theatre, name and type of page.

pins.title: Page number
pins.text: 10-9 is the airfield chart; v1 is the layout of the page.

pins.title: Elevation
pins.text: Of the airfield, in feet, as DCS gives it.

pins.title: Position
pins.text: The airfield reference point three ways: decimal minutes, degrees-minutes-seconds and MGRS to 10 m. Pick the one your navigation system takes.

pins.title: Magnetic variation
pins.text: For 1985. Every heading on the chart is magnetic.

pins.title: Tower
pins.text: Its frequencies on every band DCS gives: VHF, UHF, FM, HF.

pins.title: Navaids
pins.text: The beacons of the airfield: type, ident, frequency or channel. Part 2 tells which ones your aircraft can use.

pins.title: Beacons on the plan
pins.text: Each at its real place: NDB (dotted circle), VOR/DME (hexagon), TACAN.

pins.title: Runway heading
pins.text: Magnetic, beside the threshold where you land in that direction.

pins.title: Taxiway names
pins.text: Real names, from OpenStreetMap or read on the signs in DCS. No name: none found.

pins.title: Parking stands
pins.text: Every stand at its place. Their DCS numbers are on the parking pages 10-9A, 10-9B.

pins.title: Latitude and longitude
pins.text: One tick per minute: 37-59 is 37°59' N, 032-34 is 32°34' E.

pins.title: North
pins.text: The top of the page is the DCS map grid north; the arrow shows magnetic north.

pins.title: Scale
pins.text: In feet above, in metres below.

pins.title: Runway table
pins.text: Each runway direction: magnetic heading, length and width, threshold elevation, ILS ident and frequency.

pins.title: Parking and legend
pins.text: How many stands, how many in shelters; the three symbols below.

pins.title: Sources
pins.text: Where the data comes from. These charts are for DCS only.

use: Before the flight, copy the tower frequency and the beacons your aircraft can use (6, 7) into your radio presets.
Find your stand on the 10-9A with the number the mission gives, then plan your taxi with the taxiway names (10).
For the runway in use, the table (15) gives its heading, its length and the elevation of its threshold: your altimeter minus that elevation is your height above the runway.
Your navigation system wants coordinates? Take the airfield position (4) in the format it uses.

pages.title: Parking — 10-9A (Konya)

pins.title: Parking page
pins.text: When the 10-9 has no room for the stand numbers, they are here, on one or more pages (10-9A, 10-9B…).

pins.title: Insets
pins.text: Each frame enlarges one area; its title gives the stands it holds (here 87 to 124).

pins.title: Scale of the inset
pins.text: Insets have different scales; compare distances only inside one frame.

pins.title: Stand number
pins.text: The number DCS gives the stand, the one the Mission Editor and the mission briefing use.

pins.title: Stand type
pins.text: Open, shelter (hardened aircraft shelter or hangar), helicopter only.

pins.title: Numbers as in DCS
pins.text: Including the numbers DCS repeats at some bases.

use: Your mission gives you a stand number: find its inset by the ranges in the inset titles, then the stand.
From the stand, follow the pavement to the taxiway names of the 10-9.

pages.title: A helicopter base — 10-9 (Naqoura)

pins.title: Helicopter base
pins.text: A base without a runway is drawn on the softened F10 map.

pins.title: Pad
pins.text: Each pad circled in red at its real size, with its DCS number.

pins.title: Header
pins.text: As on any 10-9.

use: Pick your pad by its number, as the mission gives it; the F10 background lets you recognise the place from the air.

pages.title: The heliport directory (Syria, page 11)

pins.title: Heliport
pins.text: Its DCS name; the number of pads on the right.

pins.title: Pads
pins.text: Circled in red, with their DCS numbers.

pins.title: Same scale everywhere
pins.text: Every plan of the directory is at the same scale: sizes compare from one heliport to the next.

pins.title: Position
pins.text: Latitude and longitude of the heliport.

pins.title: Nearest town
pins.text: Distance and direction from a town you can find on the map.

pins.title: Split heliport
pins.text: When pads are far apart, two frames, with the distance between them.

use: The directory has an index at the end, by name. Enter the position in your navigation system, or fly to the town given and look for the pads in the direction given.

pages.title: Instrument approach — 11-x (Konya 11-1, RWY 01L)

zoom.caption: THE PROFILE AND THE DESCENT TABLE, ENLARGED

target.text: ILS OR VOR/DME OR NDB RWY 01L

pins.title: Approach name
pins.text: The beacons the approach can be flown with, and the runway.

pins.title: Equipment required
pins.text: What your aircraft must have. No match, no approach: see Part 2.

pins.title: Runway band
pins.text: Localizer, the beacons, final course and threshold elevation.

pins.title: Fixes
pins.text: Final approach fix (FAF) and missed approach point (MAPt), for each way of flying it: DME distance, or NDB bearing and timing.

pins.title: Holding
pins.text: Its altitude, inbound course and turn direction; one minute legs, max speed.

pins.title: Outbound and base turn
pins.text: The outbound radial, its limit (DME) or its time by speed category, then the turn onto final.

pins.title: Final
pins.text: On the runway axis, from the FAF down to the threshold.

pins.title: Missed approach
pins.text: Dashed, back to the hold.

pins.title: Terrain
pins.text: The relief read in DCS, with the highest points named.

pins.title: Minimum sector altitude
pins.text: See chapter 9.

pins.title: Profile
pins.text: The same approach seen from the side: altitudes at each fix.

pins.title: Descent table
pins.text: Distance from the threshold, altitude, and DME reading at each mile.

target.text: NO MINIMA — NOT PUBLISHED BY DCS

pins.title: No minima
pins.text: DCS publishes none: decide your own.

target.text: Not a real approach chart: DCS gives no procedure and no minima. Final on the runway axis; tracks offset from the runways. NDB users: same tracks on NDB KNY, MAPt at THR timed.

pins.title: Notes
pins.text: How the page was built, and the conditions for each way of flying it.

use: First check the equipment line (2): if your aircraft cannot receive the beacon named, take another page or fly visually.
Before the descent: set the beacon, the final course and the altitudes of the hold and of the FAF.
Join the hold over the beacon, leave it outbound on the radial (6), turn at the limit, intercept the final (7), and descend after the FAF following the table (12).
At the MAPt without the runway in sight: fly the missed approach (8, 13).

strings: ILS OR VOR/DME OR NDB RWY 01L

pages.title: Helicopter approach — 11-xH (Konya 11-1H, RWY 01L)

pins.title: Helicopter approach
pins.text: NDB only.

pins.title: Equipment
pins.text: A radio compass: the one beacon every DCS helicopter with radio navigation has.

pins.title: One altitude
pins.text: The whole procedure is flown at one altitude (here 4700 ft, QFE 400 m), at 80 kt · 150 km/h.

pins.title: Height above the airfield
pins.text: In metres, for metric altimeters set to the airfield pressure (QFE).

pins.title: Holding
pins.text: Over the NDB; you leave it straight ahead onto the outbound course.

pins.title: Outbound
pins.text: A bearing from the NDB and a time at 80 kt.

pins.title: FAF
pins.text: The end of the base turn; check the bearing to the NDB (QDM) given.

pins.title: Landing
pins.text: On the runway, or visually on a helipad of the 10-9.

pins.title: Timing and descent
pins.text: Time from FAF to MAPt and vertical speed for each ground speed, in ft/min and m/s.

pins.title: MSA
pins.text: In feet and metres.

use: Set QFE: the heights in metres are then your altimeter readings.
Tune the NDB; fly the hold, the outbound for the time given, the base turn, and the final on the runway axis.
From the FAF, start the timing for your ground speed (9); at the MAPt land on the runway or go to a pad visually.

pages.title: Minimum sector altitude
pages.caption: THE MSA BOX OF THE 11-1, ENLARGED

pins.title: Centre and radius
pins.text: Around the beacon named, out to 25 NM (46 km).

pins.title: Four sectors
pins.text: The minimum altitude in each.

pins.title: Bearings to the beacon
pins.text: A sector is given by the magnetic bearing **to** the beacon: coming from the north you fly about 180°, so the north sector sits under 180°, at the top.

pages.text: Each value is 1000 ft above the highest ground of the sector (2000 ft where the ground reaches 1500 m), rounded up to 100 ft, on the ground read in DCS. Obstacles are not counted. Every airfield, heliport and pad also has its MSA in the files `downloads/msa/`, even without an approach page.

steps.text: **Prepare.** Put the 10-8, 10-9, 10-9A and the approach pages your aircraft can fly into your kneeboard (chapter 1). Copy the tower frequency and the beacons into your presets.
**Start.** The mission gives your stand: find it on the 10-9A.
**Taxi.** Follow the taxiway names to the runway in use; the runway table gives its heading.
**Depart.** Check the elevation of the threshold and your heading against the table.
**Return.** The 10-8 shows what to look for; the MSA keeps you clear of the ground in cloud.
**Approach.** Pick the approach page your aircraft can fly (Part 2, chapter 11) and follow it.
**Land and park.** Back to the 10-9 and the 10-9A.

pages.title: 11.0 Overview
pages.caption: Which approach each aircraft can fly
rows: 11-x with an NDB, if the beacon is in its list
11-x on a VOR/DME or TACAN; ILS
11-x on a VOR/DME or TACAN; ILS
pages.note: Read the equipment line of each approach page (chapter 7, pin 2). The table says what the aircraft can receive in DCS; your module's manual says how to tune it.

pages.title: 11.1 Mi-24P
items: **Can receive**: NDB (ARK-15M, ARK-U2). No VOR, no ILS, no DME, no TACAN.
**Your pages**: the 11-xH, built for it: NDB only, one altitude, heights in metres above the airfield, 80 kt · 150 km/h.
**Example**: Konya 11-1H. Set QFE; tune NDB KNY 390; fly the hold at 400 m QFE; outbound 203° for 3:40 at 150 km/h; base turn left; final 017°; land on 01L or on a pad of the 10-9.
**Note**: the Doppler counts distance from a point you set; the chart does not use it.

pages.title: 11.2 UH-1H
items: **Can receive**: NDB (AN/ARN-83); VOR, localizer and glide slope (AN/ARN-82). No DME, no TACAN.
**Your pages**: the 11-xH. Where the runway has an ILS, the 11-x of that runway too, flown the NDB way (CAT A timing) with the final on the localizer and the glide slope.
**Example**: Konya 11-1H; or Konya 11-1: hold and outbound on NDB KNY 390, final on IKNY 108.90.

pages.title: 11.3 AH-64D
items: **Can receive**: NDB, its only radio navigation aid. GPS and inertial navigation.
**Your pages**: the 11-xH (ADF required).
**Example**: Konya 11-1H.

pages.title: 11.4 OH-58D
items: **Can receive**: no radio navigation aid on our pages. GPS and inertial navigation.

**Your pages**: 10-8 and 10-9 to find and recognise the place; the heliport directory for the pads (positions to enter in the GPS); the MSA files to stay above the ground in bad weather. No approach page.

pages.title: 11.5 MiG-21bis
items: **Can receive**: NDB (ARK) and RSBN/PRMG — but **by the channels of its own list**, not by the beacons of the map.

**Your pages**: an 11-x whose title names an NDB, when that beacon is in the module's list. The channel numbers are on the module's own kneeboard pages; our pages give where the beacons are and how the approach runs.
**Note**: the RSBN of the module is not the RSBN of the map files: do not take an RSBN channel from our pages.

pages.title: 11.6 F-5E
items: **Can receive**: TACAN. Its ADF works on the UHF radio only, not on NDB. No VOR, no ILS.

**Your pages**: an 11-x built on a TACAN (TACAN in the title). Where a TACAN stands on the same place as the VOR/DME of the page, as at Konya (TACAN KON 240 m from VOR/DME KNY), you can fly the page on the TACAN: radials and distances differ by about 0.1 NM.
**Otherwise**: TACAN to the field, then visually with the 10-8.

pages.title: 11.7 Mirage F1EE
items: **Can receive**: TACAN, VOR, ILS. No radio compass.
**Your pages**: an 11-x on a VOR/DME or a TACAN; the ILS where the runway has one.
**Example**: Konya 11-1 on VOR/DME KNY 111.20, final on IKNY 108.90.

pages.title: 11.8 F-4E
items: **Can receive**: TACAN, VOR, ILS. Its ADF is the UHF radio's: no NDB.
**Your pages**: an 11-x on a VOR/DME or a TACAN; the ILS where the runway has one.
**Example**: Konya 11-1.

pages.title: 11.9 A-10C II
items: **Can receive**: TACAN and ILS. No VOR; the ADF does not work. EGI (GPS and inertial).
**Your pages**: an 11-x on a TACAN; the ILS where the runway has one.
**Example**: Konya 11-1 with TACAN KON (see the F-5E note), final on IKNY 108.90.

pressure at sea level (altimeter reads altitude)

sections.heading: Appendix B — Limits and credits
paragraphs: **Limits.** For DCS World only, not for real-world navigation. No minima. The MSA counts the ground, not the obstacles. The approaches are standard patterns on DCS data, not published procedures. The aircraft table reflects the modules as documented in November 2026; a module update can change it.

**Credits.** Data: DCS World and its files (Eagle Dynamics), read with pydcs; taxiway names © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); ICAO codes from OurAirports; magnetic field IGRF-14; font Barlow Condensed (SIL OFL). Relief read in DCS: non-commercial use. DCS Airfield Charts is written with Claude (Anthropic).
